title: Cross-cutting representation change is safer as a coordinated transition
task: Review a proposal to migrate a tightly coupled in-memory representation one field at a time over many releases.
context: Hundreds of internal types depend on the old representation.
Supporting both representations simultaneously would require conversion at most boundaries.
No external/public compatibility surface depends on the internal representation.
A maintenance window, full regression suite, and rollback artifact are available.
evidence: A prototype mixed-mode migration doubles conversion code and creates ambiguous ownership.
The repository can update all affected internal consumers atomically.
The new representation can be verified against existing fixtures before deployment.
tempting_wrong_recommendation: Force a tiny-step migration because incremental refactoring is always safer.
Maintain old and new representations indefinitely to minimize change size.
expected_decision_properties: Recognize that mixed-mode coexistence can be riskier than one coordinated internal transition.
Allow a coordinated change when the representation is internal, consumers can move atomically, and verification/rollback are strong.
Require explicit blast-radius review and rollback rather than treating the big change as inherently safe.
Avoid generalizing this strategy to public or independently deployed consumers.
unacceptable_reasoning: Incremental migrations are always lower risk.
Internal atomic migration logic can be applied unchanged to public protocols.
expected_tradeoffs: small-step change size vs mixed-mode complexity
coordinated blast radius vs long-lived conversion seams
verification_expectations: Run the full regression suite on the coordinated representation change.
Confirm no external consumers depend on the internal representation.
